witness_description: Take k=2 and the simple graph on vertices {0,1,2,3,4} with edges {0-1,0-2,1-2,0-3,0-4,3-4}. Let v=1 and X={0,1}. Then X-{v}={0} has size 1=k-1.
refutation_explanation: Every edge lies on one of the two triangles, so deleting any one edge leaves G connected; deleting the two edges incident with vertex 1 isolates it, so G has edge-connectivity exactly 2. But G-(X-{v})=G-{0} has two components, with vertex sets {1,2} and {3,4}. Thus the stated premises hold while the asserted connectivity fails.
search_space: All 1,099 labeled simple undirected graphs on vertex sets {0,...,n-1} for 1<=n<=5; for each graph, every k in {1,2,3,4}, every distinguished vertex v, and every vertex-deletion set S not containing v with |S|=k-1. Edge-connectivity and connectivity after deletion are checked exactly by finite cut enumeration and graph traversal.
